passage: Supervisor's note. This week Damini, our intern, presented to the team. She talks with her whole face: eyebrows shooting up at good points, dropping low when she is serious, a lot of movement. Her colleague Ken told me afterwards that he found it dramatic, and wondered if she was annoyed at the questions. I asked Damini about it. She laughed and said her whole family talks that way, and that it means she is engaged, nothing more. Ken, who grew up in a quieter house, said his own face barely moves. I suggested they each compare with what is normal for the other person, not with their own habits. Next week I'll ask them how it went. - Tanvir

qa.q: Who found Damini's presentation style dramatic?
What might Ken have been thinking about Damini's eyebrows?
qa.a: He wondered whether she was annoyed at the questions, reading her big brow movements against his own quiet baseline, though she meant only that she was engaged.

qa.q: What did Tanvir suggest the two interns do?
qa.a: Tanvir suggested they compare each other's expressions with what is normal for that person, instead of with their own habits.

qa.q: How might Damini see Ken's barely moving face?
qa.a: She could read it as flat or disinterested, when it is just how he normally looks, so the same mismatch works in reverse.

grounding: A person from an expressive background uses large brow movements that another finds dramatic, and baseline expressiveness differs by person.

passage: Tuesday night. Third week of living with my flatmate Parveen, and I finally worked out the eyebrows. Whenever she tells a story at dinner, her brows go up so high they nearly touch her hair, then crash down when she gets to the serious bit. For two weeks I thought she was always shocked or angry with me. Tonight I asked, "Are you cross?" She burst out laughing. "No! That's just how I talk. My whole family does it." She said she'd noticed my face stays very still and had wondered if I was bored. We agreed to stop guessing. Funny how one flat face and one lively one can each feel like a complaint. - Imran

qa.q: Which week of living with the flatmate is it for Imran?
qa.a: It is Imran's third week of living with the flatmate Parveen.

qa.q: What did Imran think Parveen's eyebrows meant at first?
qa.a: Imran thought she was always shocked or angry with Imran, until asking her.

qa.q: What could Imran and Parveen do to avoid misreading each other?
qa.a: They could keep checking with a quick question and remember each other's usual level of expression instead of guessing.

qa.q: How did Parveen see Imran's still face?
qa.a: She wondered if Imran was bored, so Imran's still face gave her the same kind of wrong reading that Imran had made of her.

grounding: A person from an expressive family uses big eyebrow movements while talking, another finds them dramatic, and baselines differ.
